ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points C and D are the trisection points of line segment AB. Construct an equilateral triangle $\triangle OCD$ upwards with CD as its base. With O as the center and the length of OA as the radius, draw an arc that intersects the extensions of OC and OD at points E and F, respectively. If $AB = 6$, what is the area of the shaded region?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OA, OB, and construct $OH\perp AB$ at point H as shown in the diagram,\\
$\because AB=6$, C and D are the trisection points of the line segment AB, and $\triangle COD$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore \angle OHA=90^\circ$, $\angle COH=30^\circ$, $AC=CD=DB=2$, $AH=BH=3$, $\angle OCH=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore OH=2\times \sin 60^\circ=\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore OA=\sqrt{3^2+(\sqrt{3})^2}=2\sqrt{3}$, $\tan \angle OAH=\frac{OH}{AH}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$, $\therefore \angle OAH=30^\circ$, $\therefore \angle AOH=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOC=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the shaded part is: $\frac{2\times \sqrt{3}}{2}+\left[\frac{30\times \pi \times (2\sqrt{3})^{2}}{360}-\frac{2\times \sqrt{3}}{2}\right]\times 2=\boxed{2\pi -\sqrt{3}}$

method.method_draft: Use a synthetic area decomposition. From the image, read the shaded region as the union of the central equilateral triangle OCD and two congruent side regions bounded by AC/DB, the extensions CE/DF, and the circular arc through A,E,F,B. From the text, use AB=6, C and D trisection points, so AC=CD=DB=2, and triangle OCD is equilateral with side 2. Drop the altitude OH to AB; then OH=sqrt(3), AH=3, so OA=sqrt(3^2+(sqrt(3))^2)=2sqrt(3). method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/integral model. From the image, place AB on the x-axis with A=(-3,0), B=(3,0), so by the text C=(-1,0), D=(1,0). Since OCD is an upward equilateral triangle on CD, set O=(0,sqrt(3)). The circle centered at O with radius OA has equation x^2+(y-sqrt(3))^2=12. From the image, the left shaded side region is bounded above by y=0, on the right by the extension of OC, and below-left by the lower circle arc from A to E. The line OC has equation y=sqrt(3)(x+1). The intersection E of this line/ray with the circle is at x=-sqrt(3). Compute the left side area as the sum of two coordinate integrals: integral from x=-3 to -sqrt(3) of [0-(sqrt(3)-sqrt(12-x^2))] dx plus integral from x=-sqrt(3) to -1 of [0-sqrt(3)(x+1)] dx. Double this by symmetry for the right side. Add the central equilateral triangle area sqrt(3). Simplifying the integrals gives total area 2pi-sqrt(3).
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The diagram shows a horizontal segment AB with points C and D on it, and an upward equilateral triangle OCD built on base CD. The triangle OCD is shaded. Below the line AB there is a circular arc centered at O passing through A and B, meeting the extensions of OC and OD at E and F. The shaded region consists of the central triangle OCD plus two symmetric side regions near A-C-E and D-B-F.

Reasoning using the assigned coordinate/integral model: Place AB on the x-axis with A=(-3,0), B=(3,0). Since AB=6 and C,D trisect AB, we have C=(-1,0), D=(1,0). raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, points C and D are the trisection points of line segment AB. Construct an equilateral triangle $\triangle OCD$ upwards with CD as its base. With O as the center and the length of OA as the radius, draw an arc that intersects the extensions of OC and OD at points E and F, respectively. If $AB = 6$, what is the area of the shaded region?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OA, OB, and construct $OH\perp AB$ at point H as shown in the diagram,\\
$\because AB=6$, C and D are the trisection points of the line segment AB, and $\triangle COD$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore \angle OHA=90^\circ$, $\angle COH=30^\circ$, $AC=CD=DB=2$, $AH=BH=3$, $\angle OCH=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore OH=2\times \sin 60^\circ=\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore OA=\sqrt{3^2+(\sqrt{3})^2}=2\sqrt{3}$, $\tan \angle OAH=\frac{OH}{AH}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$, $\therefore \angle OAH=30^\circ$, $\therefore \angle AOH=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOC=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the shaded part is: $\frac{2\times \sqrt{3}}{2}+\left[\frac{30\times \pi \times (2\sqrt{3})^{2}}{360}-\frac{2\times \sqrt{3}}{2}\right]\times 2=\boxed{2\pi -\sqrt{3}}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, AB is a horizontal line segment, A is on the left, B is on the right, and C, D are located on AB and divide AB into three equal parts. Construct equilateral triangle OCD upward with CD as the base; triangle OCD is filled with shading. The arc drawn with O as the center passes through A, B, and intersects the extensions of OC, OD at E, F respectively; the curved regions on the left and right sides below AB and above the arc are also filled with shading.
Reasoning: According to the decomposition of the shading in the figure, the shaded area equals the area of the middle equilateral triangle OCD plus the two congruent side shaded regions on the left and right. AB=6, C, D are trisection points, so AC=CD=DB=2. Let H be the midpoint of CD, also the foot of the perpendicular from O to AB, then AH=3. Because OCD is an equilateral triangle with side length 2, OH=2·sin60°=√3. Therefore OA=√(AH^2+OH^2)=√(3^2+(√3)^2)=2√3. Also tan∠OAH=OH/AH=√3/3, so ∠OAH=30°, ∠AOH=60°. The altitude OH of the equilateral triangle bisects the vertex angle, so ∠COH=30°, hence ∠AOC=60°−30°=30°; similarly on the right side ∠DOB=30°. The area of the middle equilateral triangle OCD is (√3/4)·2^2=√3. Each side shaded region equals the area of the sector with radius OA=2√3 and central angle 30° minus the area of triangle OAC. The sector area is (30/360)π(2√3)^2=π; triangle OAC has base AC=2 and height OH=√3, so its area is 1/2·2·√3=√3. Therefore each side shaded area is π−√3. The total shaded area is √3+2(π−√3)=2π−√3.
